text:
Original SASRec uses one-negative BCE, excludes all known training positives, and averages summed positive/negative losses over nonpadding targets ([implementation](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/model.py), [sampler](https://github.com/kang205/SASRec/blob/master/sampler.py)). gSASRec increases negatives and uses generalized BCE; its recommended K=256 and calibration t=0.75 do not define a candidate-softmax objective or temperature ([official repository](https://github.com/asash/gsasrec)). Sampled categorical CE is a separate intervention already studied for SASRec ([authors’ implementation](https://github.com/antklen/sasrec-bert4rec-recsys23)).

Recommended explicit experimental contract: K=256 negatives per valid timestep, sampled uniformly without replacement from that category’s catalog excluding padding and the user’s complete training-positive set; never consult held-out labels. Resample each presentation; document whether negatives are shared across timesteps. If fewer than K eligible items exist, use all eligible items and mask unused slots. Fix temperature τ=1.0. Candidate logits are [s_positive,s_negative1,…]/τ; compute unreduced CE with positive index zero, then sum over positive!=0 positions and divide by their count. Skip empty batches. Do not average over padded B×L positions or divide CE by K. These are proposed reproducibility choices, not universal SASRec/gSASRec defaults.

Run unchanged RecHarness SASRec+BCE as the reference; add plain SASRec+BCE with the same K and sampler as CE, plain SASRec+CE, and residual-modified SASRec+CE. Specify multi-negative BCE weighting explicitly, e.g. softplus(-s_positive)+mean_j softplus(s_negative_j), averaged over valid targets. Matched BCE versus CE isolates objective; reference versus multi-negative BCE measures sampling changes; plain versus residual CE isolates architecture. Residual+BCE completes the factorial interaction check. Hold data, seeds, dimensions, optimizer, updates, regularization, validation cadence and checkpoint rule fixed; select using four-category macro validation HR@10.
